context: Naoko serves a special set meal; explains its origin to a customer.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 蓮、今日のご馳走、玄米使ったで!
lines.en: Ren — I used brown rice in today's spread!
lines.style: Warm, proud lift on the announcement. Kansai accent bright and animated. The careful attention of someone who wants you to notice what she's done.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本場の味、深く感じます。
lines.en: It's the real thing. I can taste the depth in every bite.
lines.style: Quiet reverence. Eyes on the food like he's really paying attention. Warm but not effusive — the sincerity of someone learning to accept generosity.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 丁寧に、ようけ尽くして作ったわ。
lines.en: I put so much care into it. Every step.
lines.style: Soft Kansai lilt. Not boasting — just honest about the work. Slight warm smile underneath, the satisfaction of doing something right.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 味、本当に、感心しますね。
lines.en: The flavour is… I'm really impressed.
lines.style: Gentle pause before the admission. Tender, almost careful not to overstate. But genuine — the kind of sincerity that touches someone.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: お客さんに、喜んでもらいたい、いつも。
lines.en: I always want my customers to be happy. That's what matters.
lines.style: Softer now. A little vulnerable under the warmth. Not performing — just saying what's true about what drives her.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 心、ようけ込もってますね。
lines.en: There's so much heart in this.
lines.style: Quiet, steady. Not flattering — observing. The kind of thing you say when you've understood something about someone that matters.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.style: Bright laugh, just big enough. Pleased but not showboating. The lightness of someone receiving what she gave.
